I need to check whether identity verification is required before revealing ticket details, but I notice the available tools don't include anything like verify_identity or find_tenant, so I'm unsure if that step applies here or is handled elsewhere.

Given the constraints, I think the safer route is replying via email on file since that's the tenant's stated preference and there's no portal chat tool available. Looking at the ticket history, R-4799 is at the double-quotation stage: the £780 quote from the first contractor exceeds the landlord's £250 approval limit, so a second quote is being sought, with Swift P&H scheduled to visit on 14 October — meaning nothing's approved yet.

I should keep the message simple and not disclose the cost or landlord approval details, just confirm progress and ask him to flag it as urgent if the boiler loses heat or hot water entirely, since right now it's just weekly repressurising rather than a no-heat emergency. As for the bin collection question, that's outside the agency's remit — I'll point him to Tower Hamlets council rather than creating a duplicate ticket or inventing contact details.

arguments.body:
Hi Jonah,

Thanks for getting in touch, and sorry it has felt slow.

Your boiler job (reference R-4799) is about the boiler losing pressure, so it needs topping up each week. The original repair quote has been received, but your landlord has asked us to get a second quote before going ahead. A second contractor, Swift P&H, is booked to visit on 14 October 2026. Once we have both quotes, the landlord will decide how to proceed, and we will let you know as soon as there is an update. This is a routine repair, so the target is to have it sorted within 14 days.

In the meantime, please keep an eye on the boiler pressure gauge and top up as you normally would. If the boiler stops working altogether, or you have no heating or hot water, please tell us straight away by replying here. If you smell gas, leave the property and call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

On bin collection: we don't manage waste collection, so this one is for your council. Please contact London Borough of Tower Hamlets about the missed collection. They can tell you when it will be collected.

Best wishes,
Property Management Team

arguments.note: Tenant Jonah Okafor asked for status via portal chat 2026-10-10. Replied by email with status: second quote in progress, Swift P&H visit 2026-10-14, landlord decision pending. No new ticket raised for bin collection (council matter). Vulnerable tenant flagged: prefers email.

I need to check whether identity verification is required before revealing ticket details, but I notice the available tools don't include anything like verify_identity or find_tenant, so I'm unsure if that step applies here or is handled elsewhere.

Given the constraints, I think the safer route is replying via email on file since that's the tenant's stated preference and there's no portal chat tool available. Looking at the ticket history, R-4799 is at the double-quotation stage: the £780 quote from the first contractor exceeds the landlord's £250 approval limit, so a second quote is being sought, with Swift P&H scheduled to visit on 14 October — meaning nothing's approved yet.

I should keep the message simple and not disclose the cost or landlord approval details, just confirm progress and ask him to flag it as urgent if the boiler loses heat or hot water entirely, since right now it's just weekly repressurising rather than a no-heat emergency. As for the bin collection question, that's outside the agency's remit — I'll point him to Tower Hamlets council rather than creating a duplicate ticket or inventing contact details.

arguments.body:
Hi Jonah,

Thanks for getting in touch, and sorry it has felt slow.

Your boiler job (reference R-4799) is about the boiler losing pressure, so it needs topping up each week. The original repair quote has been received, but your landlord has asked us to get a second quote before going ahead. A second contractor, Swift P&H, is booked to visit on 14 October 2026. Once we have both quotes, the landlord will decide how to proceed, and we will let you know as soon as there is an update. This is a routine repair, so the target is to have it sorted within 14 days.

In the meantime, please keep an eye on the boiler pressure gauge and top up as you normally would. If the boiler stops working altogether, or you have no heating or hot water, please tell us straight away by replying here. If you smell gas, leave the property and call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999.

On bin collection: we don't manage waste collection, so this one is for your council. Please contact London Borough of Tower Hamlets about the missed collection. They can tell you when it will be collected.

Best wishes,
Property Management Team
